records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ἐπὶ τὴν δεξιὰν τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου βιβλίον γεγραμμένον ἔσωθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν, κατεσφραγισμένον σφραγῖσιν ἑπτά.
records.gloss: And I saw on the right of the [one] sitting on the throne a scroll having been written inside and on back, having been sealed up with seals seven.
pieces: In the right hand of the one seated on the throne I saw a scroll. It was written on the inside and on the back, and seven seals closed it.

L.1: And I saw on the right [hand] of the one seated on the throne a scroll written inside and on the back, sealed with seven seals.

R.1: Then I saw that the one sitting on the throne held a scroll in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand. There was writing on both sides of it. It was closed with seven seals.

decisions.choice: a scroll written on both sides and sealed: Ezekiel 2 and Daniel 12
decisions.reason: Ezekiel was given a scroll written on the front and back, full of lament and woe (Ezekiel 2:9-10). Daniel was told to seal up the book until the time of the end (Daniel 12:4, 9). The scroll in God's hand most likely holds his purposes for judging and redeeming the world, which the following chapters unfold as its seals are opened.

decisions.choice: seven seals: a document closed until the one with the right opened it
decisions.reason: A scroll was rolled up and closed with wax seals, so that it could not be read until someone with the right broke them. Roman wills were sealed by seven witnesses. Seven seals here also stand for a document fully and securely closed.

decisions.choice: written inside and on the back; then sealed
alternatives: written inside, and sealed on the back
decisions.reason: The words "and on the back" could go with "sealed" instead of "written". The SBLGNT has no comma between them and most likely means a scroll written on both sides, like Ezekiel's.

decisions.choice: on the right hand: lying on the open hand, offered
decisions.reason: ἐπὶ with "right hand" may picture the scroll lying on God's open palm, held out for someone to take (5:7).

records.heading: The sealed scroll

records.source: καὶ εἶδον ἄγγελον ἰσχυρὸν κηρύσσοντα ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Τίς ἄξιος ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ λῦσαι τὰς σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ;
records.gloss: And I saw an angel strong proclaiming in a voice loud: Who [is] worthy to open the scroll and to loose the seals of it?
pieces: A strong angel was there too, and I heard him cry out with a loud voice, "Who is worthy to break the scroll's seals and open it?"

L.2: And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice, "Who [is] worthy to open the scroll and to break its seals?"

R.2: I saw a powerful angel. He called out loudly, "Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?"

decisions.choice: worthy: having the standing and right to do it
decisions.reason: ἄξιος means having the worth or standing for something. The question is not who is strong enough but who has the right to open God's scroll and carry out what it holds. The same word runs through the songs of 4:11 and 5:9, 12.

decisions.choice: open and break the seals: one act described in two parts
decisions.reason: The seals must be broken before the scroll can be opened; the two verbs describe the one act.

decisions.choice: break the seals ... open (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the breaking of the seals first, the order in which it happens (m2).

records.source: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ οὐδὲ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ ὑποκάτω τῆς γῆς ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον οὔτε βλέπειν αὐτό.
records.gloss: And no one was able in the heaven nor on the earth nor under the earth to open the scroll nor to look [at] it.
pieces: No one at all, in heaven, on the earth, or beneath it, was able to open the scroll or look into it.

L.3: And no one in heaven or on the earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or to look into it.

R.3: But nobody anywhere could open the scroll or look inside it. No one in heaven could do it. No one on earth or in the world of the dead could do it.

decisions.choice: heaven, earth and under the earth: the whole of creation, including the dead
decisions.reason: The three realms make up the whole universe as the Bible speaks of it (compare Exodus 20:4; Philippians 2:10). "Under the earth" is the realm of the dead.

decisions.choice: look into it: read what it contains
decisions.reason: To look at an opened scroll is to read it. No one could even see what God's plan held.

decisions.choice: the world of the dead (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "under the earth" stood for (m1).

records.source: καὶ ἐγὼ ἔκλαιον πολὺ ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἄξιος εὑρέθη ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον οὔτε βλέπειν αὐτό·
records.gloss: And I was weeping much because no one worthy was found to open the scroll nor to look [at] it;
pieces: I began to weep bitterly, since no one had been found worthy to open the scroll or to look into it.

L.4: And I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or to look into it.

R.4: I cried and cried, because there was no one who was worthy to open the scroll or look inside it.

decisions.choice: I kept weeping: grief that went on
decisions.reason: ἔκλαιον is imperfect: John wept and went on weeping. If no one could open the scroll, God's purposes for the world would not be carried out.

records.source: καὶ εἷς ἐκ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων λέγει μοι· Μὴ κλαῖε· ἰδοὺ ἐνίκησεν ὁ λέων ὁ ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Ἰούδα, ἡ ῥίζα Δαυίδ, ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And one of the elders says to me: Not weep; behold, conquered the lion the [one] of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, to open the scroll and the seven seals of it.
pieces: Then one of the elders said to me, "Stop weeping! Look: the Lion from the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can open the scroll and its seven seals."

L.5: And one of the elders says to me, "Do not weep. Look, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome, so as to open the scroll and its seven seals."

R.5: Then one of the elders said to me, "Do not cry! Look! The Lion from the tribe of Judah has won the victory. He is the Root of David, the king from David's family. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can open the scroll and break its seven seals."

decisions.choice: the Lion of the tribe of Judah: Jacob's blessing in Genesis 49
decisions.reason: Jacob called Judah a lion's cub and said that the scepter would not depart from Judah until the one to whom it belongs comes (Genesis 49:9-10). Jewish writers came to read this of the Messiah, the king from Judah.

decisions.choice: the Root of David: Isaiah 11
decisions.reason: Isaiah 11:1 and 10 speak of a shoot from the stump of Jesse, David's father, and of "the root of Jesse" to whom the nations will turn. In 22:16 Jesus says, "I am the root and the offspring of David." He is both David's descendant and the source of David's line.

decisions.choice: he has overcome, so as to open: the victory gives the right to open the scroll
decisions.reason: ἐνίκησεν is followed by "to open": he won the victory, and so he is able and worthy to open the scroll. The same verb is the "overcome" of the seven letters (2:7; 3:21). The victory is explained in verse 6: it was won by being slain.

decisions.choice: Lion, Root, capitalized
decisions.reason: "Lion of the tribe of Judah" and "Root of David" are titles of the Messiah, so every level writes them with capitals, as it does "Lamb" (5:6).

decisions.choice: has overcome (L, B); has won the victory (R)
decisions.reason: The same word as in the letters (2:7), and the same English at each level, so the link can be seen.

records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἀρνίον ἑστηκὸς ὡς ἐσφαγμένον, ἔχων κέρατα ἑπτὰ καὶ ὀφθαλμοὺς ἑπτά, οἵ εἰσιν τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπεσταλμένοι εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν.
records.gloss: And I saw in [the] middle of the throne and of the four living creatures and in [the] middle of the elders a Lamb standing as having been slaughtered, having horns seven and eyes seven, which are the seven spirits of the God having been sent out into all the earth.
pieces: Then, at the center of the throne and the four living creatures, among the elders, I saw a Lamb standing, looking as though {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been slaughtered. He had seven horns and seven eyes; these are the seven spirits of God, sent out into all the earth.

L.6: And I saw in [the] middle of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in [the] middle of the elders, a Lamb standing as [though] slaughtered, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth.

R.6: Then I saw a Lamb standing at the throne, with the four living creatures and the elders around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The Lamb looked as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been killed. He had seven horns and seven eyes. The eyes are the seven spirits of God, which God has sent out into the whole earth.

decisions.choice: the Lion is a Lamb that was slaughtered
decisions.reason: John hears of a Lion (5:5) and turns to see a Lamb that has been killed. The victory of the Lion was won by the death of the Lamb. Behind the picture lie the Passover lamb, whose blood saved Israel (Exodus 12), and the servant led like a lamb to the slaughter (Isaiah 53:7). ἀρνίον is the word Revelation uses for Christ twenty-eight times.

decisions.choice: standing, though slaughtered: alive, and still bearing the marks of death
decisions.reason: ἐσφαγμένον is perfect: he was killed, and the marks remain. Yet he stands, the posture of one who is alive (compare 1:18).

decisions.choice: seven horns and seven eyes: full power and full knowledge
decisions.reason: A horn stands for strength and kingly power (Deuteronomy 33:17; Daniel 7:7-8, 24), and seven is the number of completeness. Zechariah 4:10 speaks of "the seven eyes of the LORD, which range through the whole earth". The Lamb has the Spirit of God (1:4; 4:5) in fullness and sends him out over all the earth.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the throne and the living creatures, and among the elders: at the very center, close to the throne
alternatives: between the throne with the creatures and the circle of elders
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual and its exact picture is unclear. It places the Lamb at the center of the scene, close to the throne, with the creatures and elders around.

decisions.choice: Lamb, capitalized; he, not it
decisions.reason: The Lamb is Christ, so every level writes "Lamb" with a capital and refers to him as "he", with the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: slaughtered (L, B); killed (R)
decisions.reason: ἐσφαγμένον is the word for slaughtering an animal in sacrifice. "Slaughtered" keeps that force; "slain" is older English.

records.heading: The Lamb takes the scroll

records.source: καὶ ἦλθεν καὶ εἴληφεν ἐκ τῆς δεξιᾶς τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου.
records.gloss: And he came and has taken out of the right of the [one] sitting on the throne.
pieces: He came and received the scroll out of the right hand of the one seated on the throne.

L.7: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came and took [it] from the right [hand] of the one seated on the throne.

R.7: The Lamb came and took the scroll from the right hand of the one sitting on the throne.

decisions.choice: the Lamb receives the scroll as the son of man receives the kingdom
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7:13-14 one like a son of man comes to the Ancient of Days and receives dominion and a kingdom. Here the Lamb takes from God's hand the scroll of his purposes, and with it the right to carry them out.

decisions.choice: has taken: a vivid perfect
decisions.reason: εἴληφεν is in the perfect tense, which makes the moment stand out: he has taken it.

decisions.choice: the scroll (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no object; Balanced and Readable name the scroll.

records.source: καὶ ὅτε ἔλαβεν τὸ βιβλίον, τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα καὶ οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεσαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ ἀρνίου, ἔχοντες ἕκαστος κιθάραν καὶ φιάλας χρυσᾶς γεμούσας θυμιαμάτων, αἵ εἰσιν αἱ προσευχαὶ τῶν ἁγίων·
records.gloss: And when he took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell before the Lamb, having each a harp and bowls golden full of incenses, which are the prayers of the saints;
pieces: As soon as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders bowed low before the Lamb. Every one of them had a harp, and they held gold bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of God's holy people.

L.8: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each having a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.

R.8: When the Lamb took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders bowed down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Each of them had a harp. They also held gold bowls full of incense. The incense is the prayers of God's people.

decisions.choice: falling before the Lamb: the worship given to God in 4:10
decisions.reason: The creatures and elders bow before the Lamb as they bowed before the one on the throne (4:10). Revelation forbids worshiping anyone but God (19:10; 22:8-9); the Lamb receives the same worship.

decisions.choice: a harp and bowls of incense: the instruments of temple worship
decisions.reason: κιθάραν was a stringed instrument, a lyre, used to accompany the psalms (Psalm 33:2). Incense was burned in the temple, and its rising smoke stood for prayer: "Let my prayer be counted as incense before you" (Psalm 141:2). The prayers rise again in 8:3-4.

decisions.choice: the saints: all God's people
decisions.reason: ἁγίων means the holy ones, those set apart for God. In the New Testament it is a name for all believers, not a special group among them.

decisions.choice: each: most likely the elders
alternatives: the elders and the living creatures
decisions.reason: ἔχοντες is masculine, like "elders"; "creatures" is neuter. So it is most likely the elders who hold the harps and bowls.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional word. Balanced and Readable say who the saints are (m3), since "saints" in English often means especially holy people.

decisions.choice: harp
decisions.reason: "Harp" is the familiar word; the decision on its culture says what instrument it was.

records.source: καὶ ᾄδουσιν ᾠδὴν καινὴν λέγοντες· Ἄξιος εἶ λαβεῖν τὸ βιβλίον καὶ ἀνοῖξαι τὰς σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐσφάγης καὶ ἠγόρασας τῷ θεῷ ἐν τῷ αἵματί σου ἐκ πάσης φυλῆς καὶ γλώσσης καὶ λαοῦ καὶ ἔθνους, καὶ ἐποίησας αὐτοὺς τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν βασιλείαν καὶ ἱερεῖς, καὶ βασιλεύουσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And they sing a song new saying: Worthy you are to take the scroll and to open the seals of it, because you were slaughtered and you bought for the God by the blood of you out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation, \v 10 and you made them for the God of us a kingdom and priests, and they reign on the earth.
pieces: They sing a new song: "Worthy are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to receive the scroll and to break open its seals, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were slaughtered, and at the cost of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blood {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bought for God those from every tribe and language and people and nation.
You made them a kingdom, and priests serving our God, and they reign on the earth."

L.9: And they sing a new song, saying, "Worthy are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to take the scroll and to open its seals, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were slaughtered, and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blood {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bought for God [people] from every tribe and language and people and nation,
L.10: and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they reign on the earth."

R.9: They sing a new song: "You are worthy to take the scroll and break its seals. You were killed as a sacrifice. With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blood {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bought people for God. They come from every tribe, language, people, and nation.
R.10: You made them into a kingdom. You made them priests to serve our God. They rule on the earth."

decisions.choice: a new song: praise for a new act of God
decisions.reason: The psalms call for a new song when God does something new for his people (Psalm 33:3; 96:1; 98:1; Isaiah 42:10). The redemption won by the Lamb calls for one.

decisions.choice: bought at the cost of his blood: redeemed, as slaves are bought free
decisions.reason: ἠγόρασας is the ordinary word for buying in the market, and it was used of buying slaves. Paul uses it of believers: "you were bought with a price" (1 Corinthians 6:20). The price was the Lamb's blood, that is, his death.

decisions.choice: bought for God, with no object
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "you bought for God" with no object; the people bought are named by "from every tribe". Many manuscripts add "us", which would make the elders and creatures among those redeemed. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: every tribe, language, people and nation: all humankind
decisions.reason: The four words together mean every human group, as in Daniel 7:14, where all peoples, nations and languages serve the son of man. The phrase recurs in Revelation (7:9; 10:11; 13:7; 14:6).

decisions.choice: they reign (present)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads the present, "they reign". Many manuscripts have the future, "they will reign" (compare 20:4-6; 22:5). The present may mean that they share his rule now, or describe what is sure to come. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a kingdom and priests: Exodus 19:6
decisions.reason: See the note on 1:6. Here those who are made a kingdom and priests come from every nation.

decisions.choice: [people] (L); those (B); people (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names those who were bought only by "from every tribe ...". English needs an object, so every level supplies one.

decisions.choice: you, your: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The song is sung to the Lamb, so "you" and "your" take the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἀγγέλων πολλῶν κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν ζῴων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, καὶ ἦν ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτῶν μυριάδες μυριάδων καὶ χιλιάδες χιλιάδων, λέγοντες φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Ἄξιόν ἐστιν τὸ ἀρνίον τὸ ἐσφαγμένον λαβεῖν τὴν δύναμιν καὶ πλοῦτον καὶ σοφίαν καὶ ἰσχὺν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν καὶ εὐλογίαν.
records.gloss: And I saw, and I heard a voice of angels many around the throne and the living creatures and the elders, and was the number of them myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands, \v 12 saying with a voice loud: Worthy is the Lamb the [one] having been slaughtered to receive the power and wealth and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing.
pieces: Then I looked, and I heard the voices of many angels around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. Their number was beyond counting: ten thousands of ten thousands, and thousands of thousands.
With a loud voice they said, "Worthy is the Lamb who was slaughtered to receive power, wealth, wisdom, might, honor, glory, and blessing!"

L.11: And I looked, and I heard [the] voice of many angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders, and their number was myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands,
L.12: saying with a loud voice, "Worthy is the Lamb who was slaughtered to receive the power and wealth and wisdom and might and honor and glory and blessing."

R.11: Then I looked, and I heard the voices of a great many angels. They stood all around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. There were millions and millions of them, more than anyone could count.
R.12: They called out with a loud voice, "The Lamb who was killed is worthy to receive power, riches, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and praise!"

decisions.choice: myriads of myriads: Daniel 7:10
decisions.reason: Daniel saw a thousand thousands serving the Ancient of Days and ten thousand times ten thousand standing before him (Daniel 7:10). μυριάδες is ten thousand, the largest Greek number word; "myriads of myriads" means a number beyond counting.

decisions.choice: seven gifts under one article: praise that is complete
decisions.reason: One article governs all seven nouns, so they are one whole. Seven is the number of completeness: every kind of praise belongs to the Lamb. Several of the words are given to God in 4:11 and 7:12.

decisions.choice: blessing: praise, words that speak well of him
decisions.reason: εὐλογίαν means speaking well of someone, and when given to God it is praise.

decisions.choice: myriads of myriads (L); ten thousands of ten thousands (B); millions and millions (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek word. Balanced says what a myriad is. Readable uses a number young readers know, with "more than anyone could count" to say what the phrase means (m1).

decisions.choice: blessing (L, B); praise (R)
decisions.reason: "Blessing" said to God is praise (m3); Readable uses the plainer word.

records.source: καὶ πᾶν κτίσμα ὃ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὑποκάτω τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς πάντα, ἤκουσα λέγοντας· Τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ ἡ εὐλογία καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
records.gloss: And every creature which [is] in the heaven and on the earth and under the earth and on the sea, and the things in them all, I heard saying: To the [one] sitting on the throne and to the Lamb the blessing and the honor and the glory and the might into the ages of the ages.
pieces: Then every created thing in heaven, on earth, under the earth and on the sea, all that they hold, I heard saying: "To the one seated on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and might forever and ever!"

L.13: And every creature that [is] in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and on the sea, and all that is in them, I heard saying, "To the one seated on the throne and to the Lamb [be] the blessing and the honor and the glory and the might for the ages of the ages."

R.13: Then I heard everything God has made, everything in heaven, on earth, under the earth, and in the sea, singing: "May praise and honor and glory and power be given to the one who sits on the throne and to the Lamb forever and ever!"

decisions.choice: every creature everywhere: the whole of creation
decisions.reason: Heaven, earth, under the earth and the sea: nothing God made is left out (compare 5:3; Philippians 2:10-11). The praise that began with the creatures and elders now fills the universe.

decisions.choice: God and the Lamb receive the same praise
decisions.reason: The doxology is given "to the one seated on the throne and to the Lamb" together. Revelation keeps worship for God alone (19:10; 22:8-9), and here it is given to both.

decisions.choice: blessing (L, B); praise (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:12.

records.source: καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα ἔλεγον· Ἀμήν.
records.gloss: And the four living creatures were saying: Amen.

L.14: And the four living creatures were saying, "Amen."

R.14: The four living creatures said, "Amen! So be it!"

decisions.choice: Amen: it is true, so let it be
decisions.reason: See the note on 1:6. ἔλεγον is imperfect: they kept saying it.

decisions.choice: So be it (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds what "Amen" means.

records.source: καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεσαν καὶ προσεκύνησαν.
records.gloss: And the elders fell and worshiped.
pieces: And the elders fell down and worshiped.

L.14: And the elders fell down and worshiped.

R.14: And the elders bowed down and worshiped.

decisions.choice: the elders fell down and worshiped
alternatives: the twenty-four elders fell down and worshiped the one who lives forever and ever
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has the short reading. Some later manuscripts add "twenty-four" and "the one who lives forever and ever", taken from 4:10. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.
